topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing introduces grating lobes, altering the array factor. Tighter spacing increases beamforming gain but raises grating lobes, degrading performance. Optimizing element spacing balances coverage and interference mitigation, crucial for high-throughput satellites and broadband services, impacting link capacity and spectral efficiency.
reference_context: Ka-band satellite links use phased arrays for massive beamforming, requiring side lobe suppression technologies to mitigate inter-beam interference.
